title: Thermos Funtainer 10oz insulates better
text:
Thermos Funtainer 10oz insulates better. I recently bought my daughter the Thermos Funtainer 10oz with folding spoon to take soup to school for lunches, it was $16.99. It has worked well but I love all of my hydro flask water bottles so I was excited to try this. I tested them out this morning side by side. I started out by filling them both with hot tap water to warm up the metal insides while I boiled water. I dumped the tap water and then filled them both with boiling water (temp was 210 degrees). I sealed them tightly and left them on the counter for 4 hours. I then took the temperature of the water. The hydro flask water was 137 degrees and the Thermos Funtainer water was 151 degrees. I could actually see a small bit of steam coming out of the Thermos container and couldn’t see anything coming from the HydroFlask. The HydroFlask feels more substantial at first (it weighs 13 oz and the Thermos weighs 9oz), but the lid for the Thermos is bulkier and I guess that’s why the Thermos retains heat better.
Overall neither leak and my 6 year old can take off and put on the lid to both, so they are both easy enough for small kids to use. But when it comes to heat retention and price, Thermos wins.
